title: deployment-scenario-heuristics-customer-synthesis
body:
Summary:
This doc captures synthesis from three customer discovery workshops (retail recommender, fintech assistant, healthcare triage) and provides a compact set of heuristics and scenario templates we can reuse when recommending Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for rapid POCs. It is intentionally light-weight: quick decision rules, sample capacity/cost numbers, rollout recipes, and an action checklist for follow-ups.

Context and goals:
- Audience: CS + SE pre-sales / solutions engineering preparing recommendations for customers evaluating a 6–12 week POC.
- Primary objective: minimize time-to-signal while keeping production-representative constraints (latency, data residency, auditability).
- Secondary objectives: surface predictable cost envelopes, outline safe fallback paths, and define success metrics the customer can validate.

Customer archetypes in workshops (short):
1) Retail recommendations (B2C scale): 10–100K active daily users; latency target 100–250ms tail; sensitive to cost per 1k requests; can tolerate hosted but want region parity.
2) Fintech assistant (mid-market): 50–500 concurrent users; strict data residency and audit requirements; latency target 50–150ms; favors Dedicated or Private.
3) Clinical triage (healthcare provider): small user base but high compliance (HIPAA-equivalent), on-prem constraints, immutable audit trails; Private preferred.

High-level recommendation heuristics (one-liners):
- Choose Hosted when you need fastest time-to-value, no strict residency/SLA needs, and can tolerate multi-tenant resource variability.
- Choose Dedicated when predictable throughput/latency and contractual SLAs are needed but customer can accept some managed-hosting tradeoffs.
- Choose Private when data residency, air-gap, or full control over model variants/ops is a hard requirement.

Decision checklist (questions to ask the customer):
- Data classification: Is any data regulated or PII that cannot leave customer VPC/region?
- Latency SLAs: What is acceptable p95/p99 tail (ms)?
- Traffic profile: steady vs spiky; burst tolerance; percent of requests that require long context.
- Failure tolerance: acceptable outage window, and need for fallback model variants.
- Integration surface: direct DB access, k8s sidecars, SSO, KMS/HSM.
- Budget horizon: monthly commit vs pay-as-you-go.

Architectural tradeoffs and quick math: (numbers are heuristic estimates for scoping POCs)
- Hosted: good for 0–1M tokens/day, median per-token cost lowest for small/episodic usage due to multitenancy; cold-starts and noisy neighbors may add +10–50ms variability.
- Dedicated: provisioned GPU pools; good for sustained 2–50M tokens/day; predictable throughput, discount for reserved commit (20–40% vs hosted at scale).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): CAPEX or enterprise licensing; best for regulated workloads or when customer requires chain-of-custody logs; ops lift increases time to first test by 2–6 weeks typically.

Latency/cost heuristics (for early scoping):
- Example: 8k token/day of a single LLM route -> Hosted: ~$50–150/mo (small toy estimate), Dedicated baseline: higher fixed cost but cheaper per-token at scale, Private: significant setup + monthly platform fee.
- p95 overhead: Hosted +50ms, Dedicated +20ms, Private depends on network topology (on-prem LAN generally <20ms, cross-region VPC add 30–80ms).

Routing and fallback patterns we recommend including in every POC:
- Primary route: customer's preferred deployment (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Fallback route: compatible model variant in a lower-cost tier or alternate region. Keep functionally equivalent fallbacks to avoid user-visible regressions.
- Canary policy: start 5–10% traffic on new model/route for 48–72 hours with automated quality checks (per-turn BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific metrics).

Caching and batching guidance (practical knobs):
- Activate prefix/KV cache for multi-turn chat to save 30–70% token cost on sessions with repeated context.
- Use small batching windows (5–20ms) on Dedicated to increase throughput without hurting p95 for single-request workloads.

Security/compliance considerations (quick):
- Hosted: recommend customer sign a DPA and confirm region controls; enable token-level logging with redaction; integrate with customer KMS for envelope encryption when necessary.
- Dedicated: provide network isolation and VPC peering options; restrict admin plane access; offer extended audit retention for enterprise.
- Private: include HSM/KMS integration, offline key provisioning guide, and documented incident response runbook.

POC rollout template (6-week example):
- Week 0: Kickoff + data access checklist + SLA decision (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Week 1: Minimal integration (API keys or VPC peering), test harness, synthetic workload generator.
- Week 2: Model selection + prompt engineering session; baseline metrics collected (latency, correctness).
- Week 3–4: Integrate caching/batching, implement fallback routing, begin canary traffic (5–10%).
- Week 5: Full ramp to target load, run evaluation harnesses (quality/regression), cost run-rate analysis.
- Week 6: Run final review with ops + legal, handoff playbook, and recommended next steps (Dedicated reservation, Private onboarding plan, or productionize on Hosted).

Risk register (short):
- Data access delays -> Mitigation: pre-kickoff data checklist and stub data for early tests.
- Unexpected cost growth -> Mitigation: token-rate alarms + soft caps, sampling.
- Latency regressions in Hosted under burst -> Mitigation: predefine fallback to Dedicated/region and set circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Compliance exceptions -> Mitigation: escalate to security early, propose Private pilot timeline.

Workshop notes and customer voice (verbatim snippets captured):
- "We need proof the model won't leak PII into logs" -> Offer KMS envelope + redaction pipeline and provide audit snapshot.
- "If latency jumps our UX tanks; we can't wait 3–4s for a response" -> Highlight p95 targets and batching knobs; test with representative sessions.
- "We'd prefer managed but want cost predictability" -> Recommend Dedicated with monthly commit and burst policy.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Retail customer: get representative average session length distribution (tokens per session) and peak hour factor.
- Fintech customer: confirm exact certifications required (SOC2 + ISO?).
- Healthcare customer: confirm whether cross-region backups are allowed and whether de-identified backups are acceptable.

Action items (assigned):
- Liam: produce quick-resources packet (2–3 slides) summarizing Hosted vs Dedicated SLA + pricing sketch (due 2026-02-27).
- Priya: run a synthetic latency test harness for the retail scenario against Hosted and a small Dedicated pool and capture p95/p99 (due 2026-03-05).
- Marcus: prepare Private deployment checklist (network/KMS/on-prem pre-reqs) and estimated onboarding timeline (due 2026-03-03).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc lean; slide packet should be customer-facing. Save bigger deep-dive in separate Confluence page.
- When proposing Dedicated, always include a 30-day rollback option to Hosted to reduce perceived vendor lock-in.

Appendix: quick decision matrix (text):
- If data residency = yes -> Private or Dedicated (VPC).
- If latency requirement p95 < 100ms and high RPS -> Dedicated with colocated GPUs.
- If want fastest demo and no compliance blockers -> Hosted.

End of doc.
